speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the characteristics of the breast mass you've noticed, such as its size, shape, and whether it is painful or changes with your menstrual cycle?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the mass become hard, fixed to the skin or chest wall, or is there any skin dimpling, nipple retraction, or bloody discharge? REQUEST TEST: Mammogram and Breast Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography shows a smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast; Breast Ultrasound is not available in the provided data. Physical examination notes no skin dimpling, nipple retraction, or bloody discharge.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Breast Cancer. The previous diagnosis of Gastroenteritis is incorrect as breast masses do not present with GI symptoms, and the rapid growth of a hard mass warrants immediate biopsy confirmation. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the results of the Mammogram and Breast Ultrasound ordered previously.
